purpose: OPERATOR REFERENCE ONLY. This audit is not design DNA and must never seed design-reference or tokens.css. The owl template is the sole source of design truth.
strengths: Clear, benefit-led H1 that names all three counties served — good local SEO instinct.
Above-the-fold quote form with a service dropdown; the primary conversion path is visible without scrolling.
Trust badges (Locally Owned / 20+ Years in Business / Licensed & Insured) sit right under the hero.
Real, non-stock photography of the actual truck fleet and technicians — genuinely valuable brand asset most competitors lack.
Deep, well-written service pages with real technical specificity (VRF/VAV, testing & balancing, grease interceptors) rather than thin filler.
Consistent phone number placement in a sticky red header button.
weaknesses: CRITICAL CONTENT DEFECT: the 'Building and Maintenance Services in Miami-Dade & Broward County' section opens with 'We provide expert sprinkler repair services throughout Broward, FL, ensuring your lawn sprinkler system functions efficiently year-round.' This is copy left over from a lawn-sprinkler template and has nothing to do with Raircon. It sits in the highest-value body slot on the homepage.

Large blank white void roughly mid-page where the Google reviews block should render — the reviews section fails to paint, leaving several hundred pixels of empty space between the services block and the fleet photo.
Zero social proof surfaced above the fold. 4.7 stars across 219 Google reviews is the company's single strongest asset and it appears nowhere in the hero.
The 20+ years claim is stale — the company was founded in January 2002, so it is 24 years, and the copyright still reads 2024.
No dedicated per-city pages. Service coverage is expressed as three county map images in the footer, which captures none of the 'HVAC near me in {city}' search demand.
Instagram icon in the footer links to https://instagram.com — a dead placeholder.
No email address published anywhere on the site; phone is the only contact channel besides the form.
Service pages are wall-of-text with no imagery below the hero, no pricing signal, and no repeated CTA between sections.
No FAQ content anywhere, despite an emergency-service business where 'how fast can you get here' and 'do you pull permits' are the obvious questions.
No mention of permits, certificates of insurance, or HOA/condo board process — the exact friction points Miami-Dade high-rise owners face.
Eight top-level services in the nav with a deep dropdown; the taxonomy is flat and dilutes the AC/HVAC core the business is actually known for.

load_and_technical.notes: Page returns full server-rendered HTML to a plain fetch. Homepage weight is heavy (~2.3 MB screenshot at 1280x4500) with uncompressed PNG map images in the footer. No blocking issues observed.

conversion_gaps: Star rating and review count absent from the hero.
No urgency or response-time promise despite reviews specifically praising sub-2-hour arrival.
No city-level landing pages to capture local search.
No secondary CTA (call vs. form) differentiation for emergency traffic.
Reviews section broken, so the strongest proof on the page never displays.
